headline: South Asia: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages.
- India: Ukraine strikes Russian oil refinery, train in overnight drone attacks; 2 killed.
- Asia: France to protect key Saudi oil terminal as Houthis step up missile attacks.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns.
- Military Times, 21 hours ago: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns.
Unauthorized users accessed files containing the personal information of U.S. military personnel, a new breach notification letter warns.
- Military Times, 20 hours ago: 8 sailors attempted suicide aboard ships from Lincoln strike group, Cao says.
Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao confirmed that eight sailors from the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group attempted suicide.
- Military Times, 21 hours ago: Nellis Air Force Base says goodbye to last A-10 Thunderbolt II.
After five decades at the Nevada base, airmen saluted its last operational A-10 Warthog as it conducted its final flight Tuesday.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russian state news agency publishes column claiming Russia faces new "special military operation" in Lithuania.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Russian state news agency publishes column claiming Russia faces new "special military operation" in Lithuania.
Kremlin-aligned Russian outlet RIA Novosti published and later deleted an opinion piece threatening Lithuania with a Russian invasion and nuclear strike.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: ArcelorMittal shuts down Ukraine's largest metallurgical company following Russian attacks.
Ukraine's largest steelmaker, ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih, suspends operations following four missile attacks that killed five employees and injured 17.
- The Moscow Times, 21 hours ago: Regions Calling: Russia’s Got a Bear Problem.
At least 19 people have been killed in brown bear attacks across the country since April. What is going on?
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: UK companies to use Ukrainian battlefield data to train AI-powered drone swarms.
Up to 12 British companies will gain access to more than 6 million battlefield detections from Ukraine to develop AI models for autonomous drone swarms.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Zelenskyy warns $27B funding gap could leave Ukraine short of weapons.
- Politico Europe, one hour ago: Zelenskyy warns $27B funding gap could leave Ukraine short of weapons.
The president said he received a positive and constructive response from the EU during his diplomatic talks this week.
- Balkan Insight, one hour ago: Week in Review: Spyware, AI and Arrests.
Tech concerns mount over elections in Serbia, spy chief’s arrest tests Albania’s NATO ties, protests over court verdicts continue in Kosovo and North Macedonia mulls impact of dangerous virus, our selection of Balkan Insight’s Premium stories this week shows.
- Politico Europe, 10 hours ago: Deutschland und Spanien zetteln Papierkrieg zu „Made in Europe“-Auslegung an.
Berlin strebt einen breit aufgestellten Verbund von Handelspartnern an, während Madrid ein gestaffeltes System vorschlägt, bei dem in der EU hergestellte Waren Vorrang genießen.
- Balkan Insight, 23 hours ago: Bosnia Dismisses Two Soldiers for Glorifying Ratko Mladic.
Defence Ministry terminates contracts of two soldiers who honoured the legacy of convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Fighting intensifies in northern Ethiopia as Tigray rebels declare full-blown war.
- Africanews, 23 hours ago: Fighting intensifies in northern Ethiopia as Tigray rebels declare full-blown war.
Ethiopia’s army says its forces have killed 272 Tigrayan fighters and wounded 260 during a counter-offensive in Amhara. The press says the figures could not be independently verified.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 7 hours ago: Sudan: Nuba Christian and Muslim Leaders Call for End to Sudan War.
[Dabanga] Christian and Muslim religious leaders in the Nuba Mountains, spanning South and West Kordofan states, have called for an immediate end to armed violence and hate speech, urging all parties to pursue dialogue and reconciliation.
- Africanews, 9 hours ago: Ethiopian president warns of 'interference' amid renewed Tigray fighting.
Speaking at the UN General Assembly, Taye Atske Selassie blamed 'external actors' for renewed conflict in the region.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 7 hours ago: Africa: Delegates Walk Out As Netanyahu Addresses Unga.
[Premium Times] Mr Netanyahu described delegates who walked out as "moral cowards."
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Israeli teenager killed during Russian drone strike on residential building in Kyiv.
- Jerusalem Post, Ukrainska Pravda, just now: Israeli teenager killed during Russian drone strike on residential building in Kyiv.
The Israeli consulate in Kyiv and the Foreign Ministry are in contact with the teenager's family and assisting in the matter.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Fighting in northern Ethiopia spurs fears of blackout and blockade.
Tigray was cut off from the world during the 2020-2022 civil war, which killed around 600,000 people.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: US seeking to revive Russia-Ukraine ceasefire talks.
Ukraine's president added that eight regions have come under attack by Russian forces since the start of the day.
- Jerusalem Post, 3 hours ago: Israel is fighting a new war on the financial front – and it is not ready - opinion.
Settler violence has been treated as a nuisance rather than as a strategic threat that hands Israel’s adversaries ammunition on a silver platter.
South Africa - bottom line: South Africa: Zulu King Breaks Silence On Deadly Heist At His Royal Palace.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one hour ago: South Africa: Zulu King Breaks Silence On Deadly Heist At His Royal Palace.
[Scrolla] King Misuzulu kaZwelithini condemned a cash heist gang during uMkhosi weLembe commemorations, after an attack at KwaKhangelamankengane Royal Palace killed two Fidelity guards on 7 September. The King used the event, which also marked his 52nd birthday, to renew his call for KwaZulu-Natal to be renamed KwaZulu.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one hour ago: Namibia: Opinion - the Land Acquisition Saga in Namibia.
[New Era] One of the compelling factors which sent many Namibians into exile to wage the war of the liberation struggle was land acquisition.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one hour ago: Botswana: Breast Cancer Awareness Tour Underway.
[The Patriot] Journey of Hope (JoH) Botswana is hosting it's 15th Annual Big Journey tour, which is a breast cancer awareness and screening initiative. The important screening initiative comes as a result of the rise in lifestyle related diseases. According to JoH Public Relations Personnel Onica Lekuntwane, there is a real need to educate communities about breast cancer as a non-communicable disease, and to make breast screening accessible to underserved communities throughout the country.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 3 hours ago: Zimbabwe: National Crisis - Only 20 out of 63 Sewage Plants Functional Across Zimbabwe, Parliament Warns.
[The Herald] ONLY 20 out of 63 sewage treatment plants dotted around the country are currently functional, signalling a national systemic collapse of wastewater management infrastructure.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages.
Ethiopian forces battled overnight to repel an assault by Tigray rebels in the Afar region, a humanitarian source said on Friday, with reports of an internet blackout in the north of the country. Rebels in the northern Tigray region seized local airports and launched attacks into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara this week, saying they were once again in a “full-blown war” with the federal government. Locals fear a repeat of the telecoms blackout and supplies blockade imposed on Tigray during the last civil war in 2020-2022 that killed an estimated 600,000 people.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, 7 hours ago: Security forces kill several Afghan Taliban fighters in retaliatory action along Balochistan border: sources.
Pakistani troops responded to an act of aggression along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in Balochistan and killed several Afghan Taliban on Thursday, state media reported, citing sources. State-run APP reported, citing sources, that the Afghan Taliban attempted to enter the Pakistani territory in Balochistan’s Gulistan sector and carry out an act of aggression. Meanwhile, officials also reported attacks on some border posts in Pakistan. The APP report said in retaliatory action, several Afghan Taliban fighters were killed.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye mull meeting of military chiefs to assist Riyadh under Makkah defence pact: FO.
The foreign ministers of Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia discussed plans on Friday to convene a meeting of the three countries’ chiefs of staff to explore ways to assist Riyadh under the Makkah Defence Alliance, according to the Foreign Office (FO). The FO statement noted that the tripartite agreement, signed on Aug 7, stipulated that an attack against any one of its parties should be considered an attack against all parties.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: How Trump's diplomatic week exposed the limits of his power.
From his high-profile address to the UN General Assembly to his high-stakes White House summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump this week was looking to reassert himself on the world stage. But Trump’s diplomatic flurry has done little to dispel the view among many analysts of a president beset by problems at home and abroad. Those include a widening Iran war that has driven up US gasoline prices and cratered his approval ratings, while his relations with allies worsen and the AI challenge from China intensifies.
India - bottom line: Ukraine strikes Russian oil refinery, train in overnight drone attacks; 2 killed.
- Times of India - Top Stories, ABC News Australia, The Moscow Times, Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Ukraine strikes Russian oil refinery, train in overnight drone attacks; 2 killed.
Russian governor Yuri Slyusar said around 50 drones were destroyed over the region and the strike forced the refinery to temporarily suspend operations. He said there were no reports of casualties there. In Ulyanovsk, eight people were injured after another drone attack damaged industrial and civilian infrastructure, Governor Alexei Russkikh said. The region is home to a major electronics plant.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: From Ukraine to Africa, drone dog fights now a reality.
The proliferation of attack drones is prompting militaries worldwide to develop drone interception technologies. Ukraine has become a primary testing ground for interceptor UAVs and innovative technologies. Other nations, including the United States and India, are developing advanced counter-drone systems to address emerging threats. The ongoing arms race in drone technology continues to evolve rapidly with new developments.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 7 hours ago: Canada says it considered risk of US attack: How their militaries compare.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has raised concerns regarding the possibility of US military action against Canada under extreme circumstances. This remark comes amidst escalating trade tensions between the two nations. The stark differences in military budget and resources underline Canada's ongoing commitment to modernizing its defense capabilities and reinforcing its Arctic strategies, while both countries continue to work together under NORAD for North American defense.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Trump gives 'totally unacceptable' warning to Xi over China helping Iran.
Donald Trump told Xi Jinping that any assistance China provides to Iran is unacceptable during his visit. The two leaders held a closed-door meeting to discuss various critical global issues, including trade and military matters. Trump organized a state dinner attended by key US technology executives to enhance relations. The visit coincided with China's Mid-Autumn Festival, marking a time for family gatherings and festivities.
Asia - bottom line: France to protect key Saudi oil terminal as Houthis step up missile attacks.
- South China Morning Post - China, 8 hours ago: France to protect key Saudi oil terminal as Houthis step up missile attacks.
President Emmanuel Macron said France would send troops to defend an oil plant in Saudi Arabia as the Iran-backed Houthi militia took responsibility for new attacks on the kingdom. Macron said in a television interview Thursday with TF1 and France 2 that he would send soldiers and military support to help protect the Saudi port of Yanbu. Saudi Arabia came under attack from the Houthi militia on Thursday, with the kingdom saying it intercepted missiles fired towards the Red Sea port of Yanbu and...
- South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: Why did Xi and China’s first lady bring their own flasks to White House banquet?.
Amid the polished silverware and fine crystal stemware on display at the state dinner in the White House on Thursday sat the vacuum flasks brought by Chinese President Xi Jinping and first lady Peng Liyuan. The couple’s flasks, black for Xi and white for Peng, were spotted on their table during the formal dinner, signalling a subtle self-assurance as cultural authenticity met high diplomacy. Extending this everyday practice to the White House banquet was in tune with the host nation’s own...
- South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: China and the US are racing ahead on AI. Can they manage risks together?.
The United States and China must work together to establish safety guardrails for artificial intelligence, leading scholars and industry leaders said at a Singapore forum, warning that rapid advances in the technology demand stronger risk controls. Speaking at the FutureChina Business Forum on Friday, Jude Blanchette, managing director of consultancy Macro Advisory Partners, urged the two superpowers to find common ground despite escalating geopolitical tensions. “If ever there was a moment for...
- South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: Young Chinese women sew own underwear, clothes, amid frustration with fast fashion.
Frustrated by low-quality materials, careless craftsmanship, and escalating prices, some young women in China are taking matters into their own hands by learning to sew their own underwear, accessories, and handbags. This summer, a surge of sewing enthusiasts flocked to RedNote to showcase their handmade creations. Many beginners embarked on their journey with underwear, assuming it would be a straightforward first project due to its minimal fabric requirements. However, they quickly encountered...
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: N. Korea building new warships on both coasts: NK News.
- Yonhap News Agency, 2 hours ago: N. Korea building new warships on both coasts: NK News.
SEOUL, Sept. 25 (Yonhap) -- North Korea has begun construction on two new warshi...
- NK News, 10 hours ago: Lee accuses Ukraine of violating pact by revealing North Korean POW transfer.
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Thursday expressed concern over Volodymyr Zelensky’s public disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) to South Korea, saying the Ukrainian president had violated an agreement to keep the move private. In a statement posted on X, Lee took aim at the Ukrainian leader […]

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Open AI attacked Australia’s health system – and then doubled down on its negligence. The time for ‘wait and see’ is over | Kate Crawford and Edward Santow.
- The Guardian - Australia, 14 hours ago: Open AI attacked Australia’s health system – and then doubled down on its negligence. The time for ‘wait and see’ is over | Kate Crawford and Edward Santow.
Human hackers face serious consequences, and so must AI companies. There is no excuse for what happened Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast When you get sick, Medicare exists to take care of you. It sits at the centre of a health system that our prime minister rightly calls the envy of the world. It’s one of the few institutions nearly every Australian still trusts. So when an AI company threatens this system, it couldn’t be more serious.
- The Guardian - Australia, 3 hours ago: Rogue AI hacks government system for first time – The Latest.
A government database has been hacked for the first time by a rogue OpenAI agent, which infiltrated part of the Australian healthcare scheme in June. OpenAI became aware of the hack in August, but only informed the government in September. Australia’s prime minister, Anthony Albanese, has expressed his ‘extreme concern’ about the hack, which raises serious AI security concerns for governments around the world. Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s UK technology editor Robert Booth – watch on YouTube Continue reading...
- The Guardian - Australia, 7 hours ago: Pocock calls for AI safety act after Medicare breach – as it happened.
This blog is now closed Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast AI hack of Medicare exposes Australia’s vulnerabilities Technology experts have warned revelations an artificial intelligence agent hacked Medicare’s internal systems will not be the only dangerous breach of government data and have called for Australia to boost its protections against the growing risk. Frontier AI now has capability to expose those vulnerabilities at a rate quicker than we can keep up, quicker than we can patch them.
- ABC News Australia, 8 hours ago: Fishtailing caravan captured on truckie dash cam prompts holiday warning.
Dash-cam footage captures the frightening moment a caravan begins fishtailing while overtaking a truck driver in Western Australia's Great Southern region.

This briefing is compiled automatically from regional news feeds and has not been cross-referenced by an editor. Treat single-source claims as unconfirmed. I will be back with the next update.
